title: Using the holiday for staff CBE professional development
description: A practical guide for Kenyan school principals on using the end-of-year break for focused, realistic teacher development that supports CBE delivery.
body:
CBE asks more of teachers than the old curriculum did: continuous assessment, competency-level judgments, and pathway-specific content. Teachers often get little time to build those skills during a busy term, which makes the break the natural window.

The aim is a short, practical programme that respects teachers' rest and produces something they can use in January.

Start from real needs

Use evidence rather than guesswork: TPAD findings, patterns in assessment data, and what teachers themselves say they find hardest. If several teachers struggle to moderate EE, ME, AE and BE grading consistently, that is an obvious focus.

Formats that work

  • Peer-led workshops, where an experienced teacher shows a technique that is already working in your school.
  • Subject cluster sessions to share schemes of work and agree assessment standards.
  • Short online courses or resources from official sources. Check what TSC and KICD currently offer for CBE.
  • Visits to a nearby school that is doing something well.

Follow up in the first weeks of term: Development that is never applied fades quickly. Ask each teacher to try one specific technique and share what happened at a short staff meeting in February.

Keep it practical and short

A few focused days, scheduled in the final week before teachers return, beat a long workshop that people attend with half their attention. End every session with something concrete, such as a marking rubric, a moderated sample, or a draft scheme of work.

Respect the break

Teachers need rest as much as students do. Give notice well in advance, keep the schedule tight, and avoid piling extra duties on top. A programme people feel is worth their time gets better engagement than one that is simply required.
